2 You are provided with solid L, which contains two cations and one anion.
Do the following tests on solid L, recording all of your observations at each stage.
tests on solid L

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the appearance of solid L.

Use a spatula to divide solid L into two approximately equal portions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Heat the first portion of solid L in a hard-glass test-tube. Test any gas produced with blue
cobalt(II) chloride paper.
Record your observations.

Add the second portion of solid L to about 10cm of distilled water in a boiling tube. Stopper the
boiling tube and shake the mixture to dissolve solid L and form solution L. Divide solution L into five
approximately equal portions in five test-tubes.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Test the pH of the first portion of solution L.
pH = ______

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Transfer the second portion of solution L into a boiling tube. Add about 3cm of aqueous
sodium hydroxide.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Gently warm the mixture from (d)(i) and test the gas produced.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Add an excess of aqueous ammonia to the third portion of solution L.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid and about 1cm of aqueous silver nitrate to the fourth
portion of solution L.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid and about 1cm of aqueous barium nitrate to the fifth
portion of solution L.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text: What does the test in (b) tell you about solid L?

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Identify the three ions in solid L.
